There has been a trend in productions of A Midsummer Night’s Dream in recent years to portray Athens as a sexually repressive regime in which Queen Hippolyta is resentfully shackled to Theseus after he has conquered her in battle. Theatre’s – ultimately gloriously escapist – Dream, portrayed Theseus as a tyrant from The Handmaid’s Tale.

cn.t: Emily Lim's joyful, playful production wins critics over with its colorful exuberance, extravagant costumes, and generous comic energy that makes audiences giddy—though purists may balk at the cheerfully irreverent approach.
